# Sanitized split-overlay executable fixtures

These are exact UTF-8 source ranges from the local, protected live-source overlays prepared for source `2559dad2ba22257e1e9ea487775fd9d0987a913a`. `manifest.json` records each range's byte offsets/hash and its parent index/archive hash. Source snippets were reviewed for embedded credentials; no runtime configuration, credential value, IAM record, archive, or unrelated website assets are included.

The public fixture contains the actual public validation, upload session, test authorization, submission, and new adapter exports and helpers. The separate SMS fixture contains the actual deployed-source-derived workflow/notification exports/helpers and direct-message export with proposed ownership checks. The loader preserves these source ranges unchanged and compiles them in separate module scopes, using their actual Firebase v1 imports and a shared **Firestore emulator**. Unrelated bootstrap/provider accessors are replaced by throwing test boundaries. CRM transport is mocked to an invalid domain. No production provider or API calls are possible through the harness.

`npm run test:crm-split-runtime` repeats the five actual transaction/duplicate recovery cases and tests staff authorization, ownership/suppression across the two packages, immutable retry bytes, and held capture. It does not prove platform deployment, IAM, secret binding, App Check enforcement, real Storage uploads, CRM intake acceptance, provider delivery, or real trigger routing. Both runtime artifacts preserve original package/lock/config bytes; the CI harness runs on both Node 20 and Node 22 with each artifact’s exact separately installed package and lockfile (both firebase-functions 7.2.5/firebase-admin 13.10.0). The public package’s own Admin SDK/Firestore object is the fault-injection target; the SMS package has a separate Admin client against the same emulator dataset. Actual cloud cold-start, runtime configuration, and per-target deployment bindings remain separate validation gates.

Fixtures must be regenerated and their manifest re-reviewed after an overlay change; changing repository handlers alone does not update the fixtures. Existing five frontend byte checks and their App Check tests remain part of CI. Test-only branch/workflow: no deployment permissions or deploy steps.
